title: Napoleon Orbit Structure: The Doubled Outer Construction Is a Half-Turn (Period Two)
description: Iterating the single outer Napoleon construction T_out gives a period-two orbit. The doubled outer triangle T_out²(z) is the half-turn (180° rotation) of the single outer triangle T_out(z) about their common centroid g = (z₀+z₁+z₂)/3, so T_out³ = T_out and T_out⁴ = T_out². On any nondegenerate triangle the period is exactly two — sharply contrasting the parent entry's outer∘inner composition, which always collapses a triangle to its centroid. Answers the parent's first open question on the orbit structure of the Napoleon map. 17 theorems, 3 definitions, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

conclusion.summary: Iterating the outer Napoleon construction T_out produces a period-two orbit. The core fact (Tout_iterate_two_*) is the point-reflection law Hₖ = 2g − Gₖ: the doubled outer triangle is the 180° rotation of the single outer triangle about the common centroid g. From half-turn equivariance of the center map (napCenter_halfTurn, pure ring) plus this law, T_out³ = T_out (Tout_cube), hence T_out⁴ = T_out² (also as the iterate identity Tout_pow_four_eq_two). Tout_iterate_two_ne_self shows the period is exactly two off the degenerate locus, and centroid_Tout records that the centroid is the fixed pivot. All 17 theorems verified with 0 sorries and 0 axioms (only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound), no native_decide.
conclusion.implications: The orbit of the single Napoleon map is the simplest possible nontrivial dynamics — a two-cycle generated by a half-turn about the invariant centroid — so iterating the construction neither converges to a point (unlike the parent's mixed composition) nor diverges. The half-turn equivariance is constant-free, isolating the role of the equilateral coefficient a² = -1/12 to the single identification of T_out² as the half-turn. This is the n = 3 base case for the Petr–Douglas–Neumann family, where successive regular-polygon constructions reshape a polygon; the period-two phenomenon here is the cleanest instance of that reshaping dynamics.
openQuestions: Metric refinement: the two members of the orbit are congruent (a half-turn is an isometry) — quantify how the outer construction scales the original triangle and relate the two-cycle members by an explicit similarity.
n-gon orbits (Petr–Douglas–Neumann): for the regular-k-gon construction on an n-gon, is the single-construction orbit always eventually periodic, and what is its period as a function of (n, k)?

overview.historicalContext: Napoleon's theorem — the centers of equilateral triangles erected on the sides of any triangle form an equilateral triangle — has a clean complex-coordinate proof (Argand, Gauss) in which the 60° rotation becomes multiplication by e^{iπ/3}, giving the center formula napCenter(b,c) = (b+c)/2 + i√3/6·(c−b). The sibling entry napoleons-theorem-oq-03 composes the outer and inner constructions and finds they annihilate a triangle's shape, collapsing it to the centroid; its first open question asks instead about iterating the single outer construction — the orbit structure of the Napoleon map. This entry answers that question: the orbit is periodic with period two.
overview.problemStatement: Let T_out send a triangle (z₀,z₁,z₂) to its outer Napoleon triangle (G₀,G₁,G₂), where Gₖ is the center of the equilateral triangle on the side opposite zₖ. Iterating T_out, determine the orbit. Prove that the doubled construction T_out²(z) is the half-turn (180° rotation) of the single outer triangle about the common centroid g = (z₀+z₁+z₂)/3, that T_out³ = T_out (hence T_out⁴ = T_out²), and that on a nondegenerate triangle T_out²(z) ≠ T_out(z), so the period is exactly two.
overview.text: Iterating the outer Napoleon construction produces a period-two orbit. Applying it twice does not run away to ever-larger or ever-smaller triangles: the doubled outer triangle is exactly the original outer triangle rotated 180° about the shared centroid. A third application undoes the rotation, so T_out³ = T_out and the orbit cycles with period two. The centroid is the fixed pivot throughout, and as long as the outer triangle is genuinely a triangle (not collapsed onto the centroid) the period is exactly two.
overview.proofStrategy:
Every Napoleon vertex map is ℂ-affine, so each claim is a ℂ-polynomial identity; the only non-ring fact is disp_sq: the displacement coefficient a = i√3/6 satisfies a² = -1/12 (from i²=-1 and √3²=3).

1. **Centroid preservation** (sum_Tout, centroid_Tout): the displacement terms cancel cyclically, so the vertex sum — hence the centroid g — is invariant. Pure ring.

2. **Half-turn equivariance** (napCenter_halfTurn): napCenter(2g−b, 2g−c) = 2g − napCenter(b,c). The coefficient a cancels symbolically, so this needs no fact about a — pure ring.

3. **Point-reflection law** (Tout_iterate_two_*): unfold T_out²(z) one vertex at a time; the result minus (2g − Gₖ) factors as (linear in z)·(a²+1/12), killed by a single linear_combination (…) * disp_sq. This is the one place a² = -1/12 enters.

4. **Period two** (Tout_cube): writing H = T_out²(z) = half-turn of G = T_out(z), a further T_out turns H back by half-turn equivariance: T_out(H)ₖ = 2g − napCenter(Gᵢ,Gⱼ) = 2g − Hₖ = Gₖ. Hence T_out³ = T_out, assembled by rewriting — no degree-4 expansion.

5. **Sharpness** (Tout_iterate_two_ne_self): T_out²(z) = T_out(z) forces Gₖ = g (the outer triangle collapses to the centroid); contrapositively, a nondegenerate outer triangle has exact period two.
keyInsights: **Period two, not blow-up**: iterating the outer Napoleon construction does not diverge — the doubled triangle is the half-turn of the single one, so the orbit is a two-cycle pivoting about the fixed centroid.

**Half-turn equivariance is constant-free**: that napCenter(2g−b,2g−c) = 2g − napCenter(b,c) is a pure ring identity — the displacement coefficient cancels. The period-two structure is geometric, riding entirely on this symmetry plus centroid preservation.

**One fact, localized**: the displacement square a² = -1/12 enters at exactly one place — the per-vertex reflection law — through a single deterministic linear_combination; everything downstream is ring rewriting.

**Compositional, not brute force**: T_out³ = T_out is proved by combining half-turn equivariance with the reflection law, avoiding the degree-4 polynomial identity a naive expansion of the triple composition would demand.

**Sharp contrast with the parent**: the parent's outer∘inner composition always collapses a triangle to its centroid; here the single construction is far from idempotent — on any nondegenerate triangle doubling strictly differs, with exact period two.

sections.title: Definitions: the outer Napoleon self-map
sections.description: napCenter(b,c) = (b+c)/2 + i√3/6·(c−b); Tout as a self-map of triangles ℂ×ℂ×ℂ sending (z₀,z₁,z₂) to the three centers on the opposite sides; the centroid; and rfl projection lemmas.
sections.summary: Outer Napoleon construction packaged as a self-map of triangles
sections.mathContext: $T_{out}(z_0,z_1,z_2) = (\,\mathrm{napCenter}(z_1,z_2),\ \mathrm{napCenter}(z_2,z_0),\ \mathrm{napCenter}(z_0,z_1)\,)$ with $\mathrm{napCenter}(b,c)=\tfrac{b+c}{2}+\tfrac{i\sqrt3}{6}(c-b)$. Each output vertex is the center of the equilateral triangle on the side opposite the corresponding input vertex. Being ℂ-affine, all iterates are polynomial maps over $\mathbb{C}$.

sections.title: The displacement-square identity
sections.description: sqrt3_sq (√3² = 3 in ℂ) and disp_sq (a = i√3/6 satisfies a² = -1/12) — the single non-ring fact used in the file.
sections.summary: a² = -1/12, the only fact beyond ring
sections.mathContext: $a^2 = (i\sqrt3/6)^2 = i^2(\sqrt3)^2/36 = (-1)(3)/36 = -1/12$. Combined with $i^2=-1$ and $\sqrt3^2=3$, this is the lone arithmetic fact every reflection identity reduces to.

sections.title: Centroid preservation
sections.description: sum_Tout (the vertex sum is invariant) and centroid_Tout (the centroid is fixed), both pure ring — the displacement terms cancel cyclically.
sections.mathContext: $\sum_k G_k = \sum_k z_k$ because the three displacement contributions $(z_2-z_1)+(z_0-z_2)+(z_1-z_0)=0$ cancel; hence the centroid $g=(z_0+z_1+z_2)/3$ is the fixed pivot of the orbit.

sections.title: Half-turn equivariance
sections.description: napCenter_halfTurn: reflecting both endpoints through a center g reflects the center through g. A pure ring identity, independent of the displacement constant.
sections.summary: napCenter commutes with the half-turn x ↦ 2g − x
sections.mathContext: $\mathrm{napCenter}(2g-b,\,2g-c) = 2g - \mathrm{napCenter}(b,c)$. The coefficient $a$ cancels symbolically, so the equivariance is purely structural — the engine of the period-two result.

sections.title: The point-reflection law
sections.description: Tout_iterate_two_fst/snd/thd: Hₖ = 2g − Gₖ for each vertex, closed by one linear_combination (…) * disp_sq; packaged as Tout_iterate_two.
sections.summary: T_out²(z) is the half-turn of T_out(z) about the centroid
sections.mathContext: Expanding $H_k$ and subtracting $2g-G_k$ leaves $(\text{linear in }z)\cdot(a^2+\tfrac1{12})$, which is zero by $a^2=-1/12$. So the doubled outer triangle is the $180°$ rotation of the single one about $g$.

sections.title: Period two
sections.description: Tout_cube (T_out³ = T_out) from half-turn equivariance + the reflection law; Tout_iterate_four_eq_two and Tout_pow_four_eq_two (T_out⁴ = T_out²).
sections.summary: T_out³ = T_out, hence the orbit has period dividing two
sections.mathContext: With $H=T_{out}^2(z)$ the half-turn of $G=T_{out}(z)$, applying $T_{out}$ again and using equivariance gives $T_{out}(H)_k = 2g-\mathrm{napCenter}(G_i,G_j)=2g-H_k=G_k$, so $T_{out}^3=T_{out}$ and $T_{out}^4=T_{out}^2$.

sections.title: Sharpness and sanity
sections.description: Tout_iterate_two_ne_self (nondegenerate ⟹ exact period two) and Tout_zero (the collapsed triangle (0,0,0) is a genuine fixed point, showing the hypothesis is necessary).
sections.summary: Period is exactly two off the degenerate locus
sections.mathContext: $T_{out}^2(z)=T_{out}(z)$ forces $G_k=g$ (the outer triangle collapses to the centroid). Contrapositively a nondegenerate outer triangle has exact period two; the fixed point $(0,0,0)$ witnesses that the hypothesis cannot be dropped.
